basis.vllm: per-kernel decode profile at the binding baseline identity, this issue (tables/bs*_kernels.csv)
basis.mpk: committed M3-I1 per-task wall spans (opt/pertask_by_bs.csv), NOT re-measured here
basis.target_rule: beat the corresponding vLLM kernel by 20-30 % => target = 0.70-0.80 x the vLLM number
basis.caveat: MPK numbers are at the AC-3 geometry (max_seq_length 132); vLLM at 256/1024. Only the attention row is materially context-sensitive - measured at +8 % from ctx 260 to ctx 556-896.

targets.why: worst ratio at every batch size and the only one that GROWS with batch (7.4x -> 9.1x -> 10.8x). Dominates the bs16 gap.
targets.shape: 30 GDN layers; 32 value heads x 16 key heads, head_dim 128; recurrent state [32,128,128] fp32 per request (128.8 MB/token/step); decay g fp32, beta bf16
targets.roofline_reading: vLLM runs at 54.4 % of the 8 TB/s B200 HBM roof at bs16 (1.92 GB of fp32 state in 462.7 us, 1.8x off roofline) - it is genuinely bandwidth-bound. MPK at 4979 us is ~5 % of roof. This is a BANDWIDTH target, not a 20-30 % target: the roofline for the stage is 252 us at bs16.

targets.why: largest absolute gap at bs1 (3981 us/step) and second largest at bs8/bs16. vLLM issues 200 quantize launches/step and still costs 8x less than MPK's 3840 quantize tasks.
targets.shape: 200 call sites/step: 160 dense (group=128 along K; K in {2048,4096,512,1024}) + 40 MoE routed activations (scales transposed to [K/128, M]). M = live tokens (MPK pads to mbt=16).
targets.note: A 10x kernel win is implausible; the M3-I1 backlog rank-1 lever (fuse quantize into the producing task, and stop computing mbt=16 rows at bs<16) is the mechanism. Ferret should target the standalone kernel at 0.7-0.8x vLLM AND the fusion should remove most of the 200 sites.
targets.roofline_reading: The whole 200-site stage moves ~1 MB at bs1 and vLLM still spends 559 us on it - 4284x off roofline, i.e. pure launch overhead. A faster quantize KERNEL recovers almost nothing; the mechanism is fusion into the producing task plus not computing mbt=16 rows at bs<16.

targets.vllm_kernel: bmm_E4m3_E4m3E4m3_Fp32_t128x8x128u2_s8_et64x8_m64x8x32_...sm100f (FlashInfer TRT-LLM fp8 block-scale fused MoE, gemm1)
targets.why: largest absolute gap at bs8/bs16; MPK streams ~7x more expert weight than it uses at bs1 (56.4 live expert groups vs the 8 top-8 routing needs).
targets.shape: 40 layers; w13 [256 experts, 1024, 2048] fp8 block-scale 128x128; top-8 of 256; M = bs tokens routed, grid = min(num_experts, mbt*topk) = 128 groups in MPK regardless of batch
targets.note: M3-I8 v2b already cut MPK's per-layer moe_w13 wall span from 76.8 to 34.8 us at bs1 by right-sizing expert activation; that A/B is NOT in the committed pertask_by_bs.csv numbers used here.
targets.roofline_reading: vLLM at 24.9 % of roof at bs1 (640 MB in 336.6 us), 7.5 % at bs16. Roofline 83.9 us.

targets.why: the flattest gap (2.05-2.17x at every batch size) over the most call sites (160), so it is the most predictable win; 1.6 ms/step at every bs.
targets.shape: 160 GEMM sites/step, 6 distinct shapes [N,K] with A fp8 [M,K], per-token-group-128 act scales, fp32 block weight scales [N/128,K/128], bf16 out: in_proj_qkvz [12288,2048] x30, gdn out_proj [2048,4096] x30, qkv(g)_proj [9216,2048] x10, o_proj [2048,4096] x10, shared gate_up [1024,2048] x40, shared down [2048,512] x40
targets.note: At M=1 vLLM's cost tracks the K-loop depth, not the weight bytes: K=4096 out_proj (8.4 MB) costs MORE (10.7 us) than K=2048 qkvz (25.2 MB, 9.4 us). These GEMMs are latency/occupancy bound, not bandwidth bound - 25.2 MB at 8 TB/s would be 3.1 us. That is the headroom a ferret kernel can attack.
targets.roofline_reading: vLLM at 13.0 % of roof (1.34 GB in 1353.5 us, 7.7x off). Worst sites: shared down [2048,512] 44x off roofline, shared gate_up 30x, out_proj 10x. Cost tracks K-loop depth, not bytes. SGLang's DeepGEMM already takes 13 % of this with a different algorithm, so >30 % is available.

targets.shape: 40 layers; w2 [256 experts, 2048, 512] fp8 block-scale; bf16 output
targets.roofline_reading: vLLM at 13.9 % of roof at bs1, 5.5 % at bs16. SGLang's TN/noShfl variant is 24 % faster than vLLM's at bs1 (5.68 vs 7.52 us/call) - free evidence that the target is reachable.

targets.shape: 10 full-attention layers; 16 q-heads / 2 kv-heads GQA, head_dim 256, partial RoPE dims[0:64], bf16 paged KV, page size 1056, scale 1/16
targets.note: Context caveat quantified: the same kernel costs 8.706 us/call at ctx~260 vs 9.425 at ctx 556-896 (+8.3 %). MPK's number is at ctx<=132, so the true ratio at matched context is within ~10 % of the value above. MPK's attention also has concurrency 2.0 (2 tasks/layer) - the narrowest stage in the megakernel.

targets.shape: 40 layers; softmax over 256 experts, top-8, renormalise; router GEMM [256,2048] bf16 is counted separately
targets.note: MPK's router runs at concurrency 9.0 out of 128 workers - a width problem as much as a kernel problem (M3-I1 backlog rank 3).

targets.shape: 30 GDN layers; depthwise causal conv, conv_dim 8192, kernel width 4, bf16, state [3, 8192] per request
targets.roofline_reading: 243x off roofline at bs1 (2.8 MB in 89.6 us) - latency-bound, like quantize.

do_not_ferret.reason: MPK already wins by 3-4x because it fuses norms/RoPE/L2-norm into its GEMM, attention and recurrent tasks. vLLM spends 558-680 us/step on 273-312 separate elementwise/Triton launches. This is MPK's structural advantage, not a target.
parity. MPK fuses gate GEMM + sigmoid + mul + residual into one task (238); vLLM needs 3-4 kernels on an overlapped side stream.
parity or better at bs1/bs8. APPROXIMATE row - vLLM's activationDeepSeekKernel also re-quantises to fp8, which MPK bills to task 275.
only 38-49 us/step of absolute gap; not worth a ferret run.
vLLM's lm_head GEMM moves 1.017 GB of bf16 weights in 150.7 us = 6.75 TB/s, ~84 % of B200 HBM peak. There is <20 % headroom and it is a roofline, not an implementation gap.

ncu_status: UNAVAILABLE on catalyst-B200 - counter collection fails on every kernel including a trivial control; see ncu/NCU_UNAVAILABLE.md. Substituted by the analytic memory roofline in ncu/roofline.csv, calibrated against lm_head at 84 % of HBM peak.

sglang_cross_check.verdict: SGLang 0.5.16 serves the checkpoint on one B200; NOT the same kernel identity

different_backend.dense_fp8: DeepGEMM (vLLM auto-disables it here on E8M0 accuracy grounds); 0.87x vLLM

sglang_cross_check.implication: targets 1 (GDN recurrent) and 6 (attention) are measured against a reference two independent engines agree on or that vLLM wins; targets 2 and 4 have 13-32 % of slack a second production engine already collects.
